description: Critical symptom combinations that automatically escalate triage to EMERGENCY regardless of individual CTCAE grades
source: NCCN Supportive Care Guidelines; ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines; Clinical consensus

combinations.name: Febrile Neutropenia (Classic Presentation)
combinations.rationale: 30-day mortality without treatment: up to 10-15%. Blood cultures before antibiotics; empiric broad-spectrum coverage within 60 min of presentation.
combinations.citation: Freifeld AG et al. CID 2011;52:e56; NCCN v2.2024

combinations.name: Sepsis Signs in Oncology Patient
combinations.rationale: Rigors, confusion, or hypotension with fever suggest sepsis. SOFA criteria may be met. Time-critical intervention.

combinations.name: Pulmonary Embolism Pattern
combinations.rationale: Cancer patients have 4-7x increased VTE risk. Sudden dyspnea + pleuritic pain = PE until proven otherwise.
combinations.citation: Khorana AA et al. J Thromb Haemost 2007

combinations.name: Spinal Cord Compression
combinations.rationale: Malignant spinal cord compression — functional recovery depends on neurological status at treatment. Window for intervention is narrow.
combinations.citation: Loblaw DA et al. J Clin Oncol 2005;23:2028

combinations.name: Hypercalcemia of Malignancy
combinations.rationale: Hypercalcemia (most common in myeloma, breast, lung, RCC) causes constellation of GI + neuro symptoms. Corrected calcium > 12mg/dL needs IV bisphosphonates.

combinations.name: Superior Vena Cava Syndrome
combinations.rationale: SVC syndrome from mediastinal tumor or thrombosis. Respiratory distress may develop rapidly.

combinations.name: Tumor Lysis Syndrome Risk
combinations.rationale: TLS within 72h of chemotherapy initiation. Hyperuricemia, hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia — can cause fatal arrhythmia or renal failure.
combinations.citation: Cairo MS, Bishop M. Br J Haematol 2004;127:3

combinations.name: Neutropenic Enterocolitis (Typhlitis)
combinations.rationale: Typhlitis/neutropenic enterocolitis — 50% mortality without rapid surgical + medical management. Febrile neutropenia + RLQ pain requires CT abdomen urgently.
combinations.citation: Gorschlüter M et al. Leuk Lymphoma 2005;46:651
